lessons.title: What Counts as a Capital Asset and When a Gain Becomes Taxable

body.text: Capital gains tax is not a tax on owning something that has gone up in value. It is a tax on transferring it. No capital asset, or no transfer, means no capital gain.

children.text: Meet Priya, a 29-year-old product analyst in Pune. In one year she sells 100 Infosys shares on Zerodha, sells her old Hyundai i20, inherits her grandmother's gold bangles and switches her mutual fund from the regular plan to the direct plan. Four events, and only some of them create a capital gain. By the end of this lesson you will be able to sort them in seconds.

Every capital gains question in this course starts with the same two tests. First, is the thing a capital asset? Second, has it been transferred? Only when both answers are yes do you move on to holding periods, cost and tax rates.
Test 1: Is It a Capital Asset?

markDefs.definition: Property of any kind held by a person, whether or not connected with business or profession, other than specific exclusions such as stock-in-trade, personal effects and rural agricultural land. Defined in section 2(22) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (section 2(14) of the 1961 Act).

children.text: The Income-tax Act, 2025, which replaced the 1961 Act from 1 April 2026, defines a
capital asset

in section 2(22) (section 2(14) of the 1961 Act). The starting point is deliberately wide: property of any kind that you hold, whether or not it is connected with your job or business. Then the law carves out a short list of exclusions.

body.text: Remember the structure, not a long list. Everything you own is a capital asset unless it falls into an exclusion. So the smart question is never "is this included?" but "is this excluded?"

children.text: The Main Exclusions
Stock-in-trade:
goods or securities held as inventory of a business. A jeweller's gold stock or a full-time trader's trading book is business income, not capital gains.
Personal effects:
movable property held for personal use by you or a dependent family member, such as your car, phone, furniture, clothes and home appliances.
Rural agricultural land in India:
farmland outside the notified distance from a municipality. Urban agricultural land stays a capital asset.
A few specified government gold instruments:
older gold bond schemes and deposit certificates under gold deposit and gold monetisation schemes.

body.text: The personal effects exclusion has its own exclusions. Jewellery, archaeological collections, drawings, paintings, sculptures and any work of art are capital assets even if you hold them purely for personal use. Your grandmother's gold bangles are a capital asset. Your car is not.

body.title: Capital Asset or Not? The Everyday Split

columns.label: Capital Assets
points: Listed shares held in your demat account (Reliance, Infosys, HDFC Bank)
Equity, debt and hybrid mutual fund units, ETFs like Nippon India ETF Nifty BeES
Gold jewellery, gold coins, Gold ETFs and Sovereign Gold Bonds
A flat, plot or shop, even if you live in it
Unlisted shares, ESOP shares after allotment, US stocks
Paintings, sculptures and other art, even if displayed at home

columns.label: Not Capital Assets
points: Your personal car, scooter or bike
Furniture, clothes, phones, laptops and appliances for personal use
Stock-in-trade of a business, including a trader's trading inventory
Specified government gold deposit certificates and older gold bond schemes

body.title: Spot the Non-Capital Asset
body.question: Rohan, a salaried engineer in Hyderabad, owns the four items below. Which one is NOT a capital asset for him?
options: A gold chain he wears every day
The Maruti Swift he drives to office
A painting by a local artist hanging in his living room
Units of an equity mutual fund bought through Groww
body.explanation: His car is movable property held for personal use, so it is a personal effect and falls outside the definition. The gold chain and the painting are also held for personal use, but jewellery and works of art are specifically carved back in as capital assets. Mutual fund units are always capital assets for an investor.

body.title: Deep Dive: When Is Agricultural Land "Urban"?

children.text: Agricultural land is a capital asset if it lies inside a municipality or cantonment board with a population of 10,000 or more, or within the aerial distance below from the local limits of such a municipality. Population is taken from the last census figures published before the first day of the tax year.

content.caption: Distance test for agricultural land (measured aerially from municipal limits)
headers: Land Is a Capital Asset If Within

cells: Not urban on account of this municipality

children.text: So farmland 5 km outside Nashik (population well above 10 lakh) is a capital asset and its sale can attract capital gains tax. Farmland 5 km from a small town of 60,000 people is rural and outside capital gains altogether.
Test 2: Has There Been a Transfer?

markDefs.definition: Defined in section 2(109) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (section 2(47) of the 1961 Act). Includes sale, exchange, relinquishment, extinguishment of rights and compulsory acquisition of a capital asset, among other events.

children.text: Owning an appreciating asset is not taxable. Section 67 of the 2025 Act (section 45 of the 1961 Act) charges tax only on profits arising from the
transfer
of a capital asset. Transfer is defined in section 2(109) (section 2(47) of the 1961 Act) and it is wider than a simple sale.

cells: Selling 50 TCS shares on NSE through Zerodha
Swapping your old flat for a new flat with a builder in a redevelopment deal
Redeeming mutual fund units, or switching from the regular plan to the direct plan of the same scheme
Giving up your share in an inherited family property in favour of a sibling for money
Shares cancelled under a court-approved capital reduction where you receive payment
Land acquired by the government for a highway project

body.label: When the Gain Is Taxed
body.value: In the tax year of transfer
body.context: The gain is income of the tax year (1 April to 31 March) in which the transfer happens, not the year you actually receive or spend the money. Sell shares on 30 March 2027 and the gain belongs to tax year 2026-27, even though the money settles in April.

body.title: Regular to Direct: Is It a Transfer?
body.textWithBlank: Switching your holding from the regular plan to the direct plan of the same mutual fund scheme is treated as a ___ of units, so any gain on the old units is taxable in that tax year.
body.explanation: A switch is a redemption of units in one plan and a fresh purchase in another. Regular and direct plans are separate options with different NAVs, so the switch is a transfer and gains on the redeemed units are taxable. The holding period for the new units starts afresh from the switch date.

children.text: What Is Not a Transfer
Section 70 of the 2025 Act (section 47 of the 1961 Act) lists transactions that are not treated as transfers. For individuals, three matter most.

stats.label: Gift
stats.context: An individual gifting shares, gold or property is not taxed on any gain at the time of the gift

stats.label: Will
stats.context: Assets passing under a will are not a transfer by the deceased

stats.label: Inheritance
stats.context: Inheriting your parents' flat or shares creates no capital gain on inheritance

body.text: Not a transfer does not mean tax-free forever. When the person who received the gift or inheritance eventually sells, the gain is computed using the previous owner's cost and, broadly, the previous owner's holding period. The tax is deferred, not erased. Chapter 1, Lesson 3 covers how that cost works. Gifts can also be taxable in the receiver's hands as income from other sources unless the giver is a relative or another exemption applies, which is a separate rule from capital gains.

children.text: Two more non-events trip people up. Moving shares from your Zerodha demat to your own Groww demat is not a sale, because ownership does not change. And a paper gain, however large, is not taxed. If your Reliance shares are up ₹5 lakh and you do not sell, there is no capital gain to report.

body.title: Your First Gain
body.prompt: Priya bought 100 Infosys shares at ₹1,450 each and sold all of them at ₹1,620 each. Ignoring brokerage and other charges, what is her capital gain in rupees?
body.explanation: Sale value is 100 × ₹1,620 = ₹1,62,000. Cost is 100 × ₹1,450 = ₹1,45,000. Gain = ₹1,62,000 minus ₹1,45,000 = ₹17,000. Lesson 3 of this chapter adds brokerage, STT treatment and other expenses to this calculation. Prices here are for illustration.

children.text: Priya's Year, Sorted

body.title: Priya's Tax Year 2026-27: Which Events Create a Capital Gain?

events.title: Sells 100 Infosys shares on Zerodha
events.description: Capital asset and a sale. Capital gain arises in tax year 2026-27.

events.title: Sells her personal Hyundai i20
events.description: A car used personally is a personal effect, not a capital asset. No capital gain, and no capital loss she can claim either.

events.title: Inherits her grandmother's gold bangles
events.description: Jewellery is a capital asset, but inheritance is not a transfer. No tax now. Gain will be computed if and when she sells.

events.title: Switches from regular to direct plan of her flexi cap fund
events.description: Mutual fund units are capital assets and a switch is a redemption. Capital gain arises on the redeemed units.

events.title: Moves her shares from Zerodha to Groww
events.description: Same owner, different depository account. Not a transfer, no capital gain.

body.title: The Gifted Shares
body.scenario: In 2023, Anjali's father gifted her 200 Asian Paints shares from his demat account. She is 32 and financially independent. In August 2026 she sells all 200 shares on NSE for ₹4,80,000.
body.prompt: Was the 2023 gift taxed as a capital gain? Is the 2026 sale taxed, and in whose hands and which tax year?
body.modelAnswer: The 2023 gift was not a transfer for capital gains purposes, because a gift by an individual falls within the "not a transfer" list, so her father paid no capital gains tax. The gift is also not taxable as income in Anjali's hands, because a father is a relative for the gift rules. The August 2026 sale is a transfer of a capital asset, so a capital gain arises in Anjali's hands in tax year 2026-27. Her cost will be based on her father's original purchase cost, and her holding period will include the period her father held the shares. Because Anjali is an adult daughter, the income is not clubbed back with her father.

body.label: Check Your Annual Information Statement (AIS)
body.description: Log in to the Income Tax e-filing portal and open AIS. Sales of shares and mutual fund units reported by brokers, depositories and fund houses appear here, so the department already knows about most of your transfers.

cards.definition: Property of any kind you hold, except exclusions like stock-in-trade, personal effects and rural agricultural land. Section 2(22), 2025 Act (old 2(14)).
Movable property for personal use, like a car or furniture. Jewellery and works of art are not personal effects for this purpose.
Business inventory. Its sale gives business income, not capital gains.
Sale, exchange, redemption, relinquishment, extinguishment of rights or compulsory acquisition. Section 2(109), 2025 Act (old 2(47)).
The 2025 Act's replacement for "previous year": the 1 April to 31 March year in which income is earned and taxed.
A gain on paper on an asset you still hold. Not taxed until you transfer the asset.

body.title: Build Your Own Transfer List for This Tax Year
steps: Download your tax P&L from your broker (Zerodha Console, Groww, Upstox) and note every share and ETF sale
Pull your consolidated account statement from CAMS or KFintech and mark every redemption and switch
Note any sale of gold jewellery, coins, Gold ETFs or Sovereign Gold Bonds
List any property, land or unlisted share sale, including redevelopment swaps
Separately list gifts and inheritances received, with the previous owner's purchase details, for future use
Ignore sales of your car, phone and household items, which are personal effects

points: Capital gains tax needs two things: a capital asset and a transfer of that asset
A capital asset is property of any kind you hold, minus exclusions like stock-in-trade, personal effects and rural agricultural land
Jewellery, paintings, sculptures and works of art are capital assets even when held for personal use
Transfer covers sale, exchange, redemption, switches, relinquishment and compulsory acquisition, and the gain is taxed in the tax year of transfer
Gifts, wills and inheritance are not transfers, but the tax is deferred to the eventual sale, not erased
Paper gains and moving shares between your own demat accounts do not create a capital gain
